summary.one_liner: Plain Pasta is a discontinued, tiny Mac menu bar app that watches the clipboard and strips styling from copied text so only plain text is pasted.
summary.what_it_does: The app sits in the macOS menu bar and monitors the clipboard for text. When text is copied, it removes formatting and puts plain text back on the clipboard, which makes "Paste and Match Style" the default behavior. The README says it was built because the author rarely wants styling copied along with text. The author states it is no longer under active development, and the repository is kept for reference. A separate branch named 2.0.0-beta holds unfinished work on a major update. The README also notes the app is available from the Mac App Store and that PRs are welcome. Contributors must clone the repo and initialize the VerifyNoBS git submodule.
use_cases: strip formatting from copied text on a Mac
make paste match style by default
remove styling when pasting web text
notable: Menu bar app that automatically converts clipboard text to plain text
Makes Paste and Match Style the default copy/paste behavior
Clipboard monitoring code based on klipsustreamer by Toni Lähdekorpi
Inspired by the FormatMatch app by Robert Wessels
Points users to Pure Paste by Sindre Sorhus as an actively maintained alternative
caveats: Official distribution is through the Mac App Store
